subject: general
question: Which of the following after fertilisation grows rapidly and ripens to form a fruit. Meanwhile, the petals, sepals, stamens, style and stigma may shrivel and fall off?
solution:
The Correct answer is __**Ovary**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• After **fertilisation**, the **ovary** begins to grow rapidly and undergoes transformations to eventually form the **fruit**.
 
• The **ovary** is a reproductive organ in flowering plants (angiosperms) that encloses the **ovules**.
 
• Once fertilisation occurs, the ovules develop into **seeds**, and the surrounding ovary tissues mature into the **fruit.**
 
• The petals, sepals, stamens, style, and stigma typically **shrivel and fall off** as they are no longer required for reproductive processes.
 
• The transformation of the ovary into fruit ensures the protection and dispersal of the **seeds.**
 
• This process is critical for the plant’s life cycle and plays a vital role in ensuring **reproduction and survival.**
 
• Examples of ovary-to-fruit transformation include the development of **mangoes, apples, tomatoes, and oranges.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Ovule**__

 __
 
• The **ovule** is the structure within the ovary that develops into a **seed** after fertilisation.
 
• It contains the **female gametophyte** and is the site of fertilisation by the male gamete.
 
• While the ovule itself becomes the seed, it does not grow into the fruit.
 
 
 
• **Gynoecium**__
 __
 
• The **gynoecium** refers to the collective term for the **female reproductive structures** in a flower, including the ovary, style, and stigma.
 
• While it plays a role in reproduction, only the **ovary** undergoes transformation to form the fruit.
 
 
 
• **Pistil**__
 
 
• The **pistil** is the single or compound unit of the gynoecium. It includes the **ovary, style, and stigma**.
 
• While it aids in reproduction, the pistil as a whole does not grow into a fruit; only the **ovary** does.
